clue.text: Masonic chief, a character from Ibsen

definitions.meaning: a senior mason or head of a building works, the top craftsman among masons
Halvard Solness, the title figure of Ibsen's 1892 play about an ageing architect

explanation.definitionFit: Both a head mason and the hero of an Ibsen drama go by this title of the chief constructor.

clue.text: In French sea shanty the King's son is a wealthy trader

parts.note: mer is French for sea
a sea shanty is a chant, a sailors' work song
a prince is the son of a king

explanation.surface: In a French sailors' song, the royal heir is a rich merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, powerful businessman is called this, a magnate of commerce.

clue.text: Dials number in Holborn

parts.note: the London district of the ...-way road junction, near Holborn, is named for a count of sundials

explanation.surface: A phone number is dialled in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven Dials is a road junction in London's West End, near Holborn, named after a pillar with sundials.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a numeral; the London junction named after its sundials puts one before 'Dials'.

clue.text: Apollo coming home lacking imagination

definitions.meaning: an Apollo spacecraft returning from the Moon is heading back to our planet
dull and prosaic, unable to soar above the everyday

explanation.definitionFit: Heading toward our planet, and also stolid, pedestrian, tied to the mundane.

clue.text: Poet shot by oarsman

definitions.meaning: a rower shoots, or speeds under, the spans that cross a river

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges, Poet Laureate, shares his surname with river crossings a rowing crew passes beneath.

clue.text: Sets off following the match

parts.note: reads as trouble after a football game, but means sets alight once a match is struck

explanation.surface: Fans start trouble after the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something after striking a match is to kindle it.

clue.text: Author cut short in council

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Alexandre Dumas, French author of The Three Musketeers

explanation.surface: A writer is curtailed at a committee meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma was the Russian legislative assembly, a parliament or council.

clue.text: Cabinet moves for a new deal

definitions.meaning: a prime minister moving ministers between posts in government
mixing playing cards again before dealing anew

explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of ministerial posts, and shuffling the pack again for another hand.

clue.text: Bishop's freedom of movement is all-embracing

definitions.meaning: a chess bishop moves diagonally over the whole chessboard
applying to everyone or everything without exception

explanation.definitionFit: A chess bishop's long diagonal sweep, and an idiom for applying to every case universally.

clue.text: Centre spread has the story of Cinderella's midnight fate

indicators.note: the centre of a word means its middle letters, here taken from the word spread

parts.note: a version is one account or telling of a story

explanation.surface: A magazine's middle pages carry the fairy tale of Cinderella turning back at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' picks RE, the middle two letters of 'spread'; 'Centre spread' poses as a magazine's middle pages.
explanation.definitionFit: At midnight Cinderella returns to her former rags, and a return to an earlier state is the meaning.

clue.text: "Oh, the brave of a distant drum!" (Fitzgerald)

definitions.text: "Oh, the brave of a distant drum!" (Fitzgerald)

parts.words: "Oh, the brave of a distant drum!" (Fitzgerald)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Edward FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: supply the missing noun of the line

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in FitzGerald's line is the sound a far-off drum makes, a word for melody.

clue.text: Premonition that vandal is coming to church

parts.note: the Huns, like the Vandals, were barbarian destroyers, so a vandal can be a Hun

explanation.surface: A churchgoer senses trouble when a vandal turns up at the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A premonition is a gut feeling or intuition about what will happen.

clue.text: Barbarian acquired a horse

parts.note: got is the past tense of get, meaning acquired
H is short for horse, as in horsepower or the slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A barbarian warrior has got hold of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were a Germanic people who sacked Rome, a byword for uncivilised invaders.

clue.text: A stately beauty, half native charm, half common sense?

indicators.note: half, said of each item in turn, keeps only the first half of each word named

parts.note: a juju is a West African fetish or magic charm
nous is British slang for practical good sense

explanation.surface: A dignified beauty seems part tribal magic, part plain good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' (said twice) keeps the front of JUJU, a West African charm, and of NOUS, slang for gumption.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman queen of the gods gives us 'Junoesque' for a tall, imposing woman of regal looks.

clue.text: Putting on the first of the greens, with pin out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged
only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A golfer putts on the green after the flag is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles T (from 'the first of the') with GREENS and PIN; the golf picture of putting is a decoy for 'staging a show'.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a play is staging it, showing it to the public.

clue.text: Name missiles in contracts

parts.note: arrows are missiles shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A list names the weapons covered in arms agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows is a verb meaning becomes tighter or smaller, a sense of the verb contracts.

clue.text: Urge Liz on to move summer visitor

indicators.note: letters made to move are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone presses Liz to get going during a summer stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrush of upland Britain that arrives from Africa for the breeding season, a migrant bird.

clue.text: Reprimands after messing about in a boat

indicators.note: says the shuffled letters go inside the abbreviation for a boat

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a common abbreviation for a boat

indicators.note: messing about with letters means jumbling them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets told off after fooling around in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' poses as idling on the water but rearranges the letters of 'after'; 'in' sets that jumble inside the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is, as well as to machine-gun from the air, an informal word for telling someone off severely.

clue.text: Last letter dispatched from pirates' place shows regret for wrong-doing

indicators.note: dispatched means sent away, so that letter is removed from the place name

parts.note: Penzance, a Cornish town, from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Sending a final letter from a pirate's haunt shows remorse for crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; Penzance is a town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken as a sign of sorrow and contrition for sin.

clue.text: Produce manifest

definitions.meaning: to bring out and show, as evidence in court
to display or show clearly, as a quality

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to show or display openly, as a verb.

clue.text: Ask earnestly for office of bishop in live church

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a see is a bishop's diocese or seat of office

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a bishopric in a lively church.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or beg urgently.

clue.text: They cause disease current in man, one concludes

indicators.note: concludes says the numeral one comes at the end
says the current goes inside the man's name

parts.note: Bill is a man's name
AC is alternating current
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Current flowing in a man finishes him off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod-shaped bacteria, some of which are pathogens.

clue.text: I arrange money for a pin-up

parts.note: to do the flowers or hair is to arrange them
L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out the cash to pay for a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the old abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is someone much admired or idolised, a heart-throb.

clue.text: Stylish cape, classical here

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
hic is Latin, the classical language, for here

explanation.surface: A fashionable cloak in a classic cut is found here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means elegant and fashionable.

clue.text: Bwana becoming big landowner in India

indicators.note: one word becoming another means its letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An African master turns into an Indian grandee.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim ruler or wealthy man of rank in Mughal India.

clue.text: Woman is about to go round for more sage

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A woman wants to fetch more of a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage as an adjective means wise, so more sage is more knowing.

clue.text: Joiner, comfortably situated

definitions.meaning: ... the joiner is one of the rustic players in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's carpenter in the Dream, and an adjective for cosy and secure.

clue.text: Cheat, relatively speaking

indicators.note: says the family word is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: said of a relative, taken as a cousin, one of the family

explanation.surface: Someone is a swindler, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' points to a relative, a cousin, whose spoken form matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cozen is an old word for to deceive or trick.

clue.text: Cat is able to swim in this region -

indicators.note: a swimming jumble means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat manages to swim in these waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of water bordered by Sweden, Finland, Poland and the Baltic states.

clue.text: Answer touched on what to call Hornung's hero

parts.note: in crosswords a light is an answer in the grid
fingered means touched with the fingers

explanation.surface: A solution prodded at a description of E W Hornung's famous character.
explanation.walkthrough: E W Hornung created Raffles, the gentleman burglar; 'light' is crossword jargon for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles was a cricketer and cat burglar, so he is given to thieving, adept at stealing.
